title: John Somer ("Mr. Lomer") to Secretary Cecil, Paris, 9 December 1563, BL Add MS 4136 ff. 138-139 (DECODE R9235)

plaintext.source: CSP Foreign vi (1869) no. 1471 (calendar summary of the deciphered original)

transcription.source: DECODE images (Forbes's copy of the ciphered passages)
transcription.notes: Passages (1)-(10) on ff.138-139; only passage (1) lines 2-3 transcribed for the key check. f.138 top ends a Throckmorton letter; f.139 (11)-(17) marked Sr Tho: Smith.

system.summary: Throckmorton's third cipher (R9262 p.1): homophonic alphabet of dotted digits and signs, word signs (τ = the), clear-word nulls (car, hault, bab…). Checked on passage (1).
system.notes: Key from the archive (R9262); not Smith's key R9261.

prior_solution.where: Calendar of State Papers, Foreign, Elizabeth vi (1869), no. 1471 ("Portions in cipher, deciphered")

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched R9235 (2 images) and metadata with the shared DECODE cookie.
Record is composite: Throckmorton (41)-(54), Somer (1)-(10) signed J. Somer, Smith (11)-(17). "Lomer" = Somer.
Smith's key R9261 compared: different signs. Clear nulls (car, hault, quant, apres) point to Throckmorton's third cipher R9262.
CSP Foreign vi Nov-Dec 1563 pages searched for Somer: no. 1471, Paris 9 Dec 1563, portions in cipher, deciphered.
Applied R9262 values to passage (1): "from the French ambassador advertised the same", matching CSP §3.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): the two lines of passage (1) checked against the key (transcription_p1.txt) and the CSP Foreign vi no. 1471 calendar summary (csp_vi_1471.txt); the rest of the cipher was not transcribed and the contemporary decipherment is at Cecil's office, not in the folder (project work)

outcome.method_basis: The letter was deciphered at the time and calendared in CSP Foreign vi no. 1471 ('Portions in cipher, deciphered'); the project identified the key as Throckmorton's third cipher (DECODE R9262) and checked it on passage (1) only.
outcome.notes: Deciphered at the time; calendared CSP Foreign vi no. 1471. Catalogue entry 95 removed, no write-up.

texts.summary: John Somer, Sir Thomas Smith's secretary (the 'Mr. Lomer' of DECODE), to Secretary Cecil from Paris, in Throckmorton's third cipher: his crossing from Dover, the fortification of the citadel at Calais, and the French ambassador De Foix's reports. Deciphered at the time and calendared in CSP Foreign vi (1869) no. 1471.
